_readme: MONEY-1357 — the realtime socket holder's liveness.
This is the ONE monitor in the set where notify_no_data is deliberately TRUE,
and the reason is a property of the process rather than a preference.
tiingo-realtime is a singleton: minScale = maxScale = 1, one WebSocket, one
Redis leader lock, `cpu-throttling: false` so it is not starved between
requests. Everything else in this estate is either horizontally scaled or
runs on a clock. For those, silence is ambiguous — an idle night looks like a
dead job — which is why every other row here sets it false and lets a
zero-write or absence monitor speak instead.
Here silence is UNAMBIGUOUS. `rt.health_ok` is emitted from flushTick's
`finally`, every FLUSH_MS (5s), on every path including the early returns for
not-leader and nothing-due. There is no state in which a living process stops
emitting it. So no points means the process is gone, and that is exactly the
_threshold_rationale: `min` over the window, not `avg`. The gauge is 0 or 1, so an average is a
duty cycle — a service that flapped for half the window reads 0.5, which no
threshold expresses honestly. `min < 1` means 'was it EVER unhealthy in these
ten minutes', which is the question.
Ten minutes is deliberately longer than one reconnect cycle.
`decideHealth` already tolerates a normal disconnect (the backoff ladder is up
to 60s and the heartbeat watchdog 45s, hence UNHEALTHY_AFTER_MS = 180s), so a
healthy reconnect never reports 0 in the first place. The window is not there
to absorb that; it is there so a single unhealthy sample during a deploy
no_data_timeframe 20 minutes = 4x the 5s emit interval expressed generously.
A Cloud Run revision swap takes a minute; 20 minutes is comfortably past any
deploy and still notices a dead holder inside a market half-hour.
name: [{{env}}] tiingo-realtime — unhealthy, or silent
message:
tiingo-realtime reported UNHEALTHY, or stopped reporting at all.

Silence is the more serious reading. `rt.health_ok` is emitted every 5 seconds from flushTick's `finally` — on every path, including not-leader and nothing-due — so a living process cannot stop emitting it. No data means the process is gone.

This is the one service where that inference is safe: one socket, one process, minScale=maxScale=1. While it is down NO US quote or minute bar is written, and the web path silently falls back to the EOD close wearing an honest badge that says so — so nothing else will alert.

Check, in order: `/health` on the service (it returns 503 with a `reason` when the leader has no working socket); the `[tiingo-rt]` log lines for `stepping down` or `disconnected`; and whether two revisions are overlapping, since the Redis leader lock is fail-CLOSED and a lock it cannot reach means no leader at all.

The `reason` tag carries `decideHealth`'s verdict with digits collapsed to `#`, so it groups.

@{{notify}}
